issue: pam/PAM contains only 48 of 1,306 catalogue endpoints (3.7% strict; 3.0% by verbatim route literal; 27.0% on the most generous text-match upper bound). It cannot be used to enumerate, schema-derive or generate tests for the API under test.
recommended_solution: Stop treating pam/PAM as the API contract. Enable Swashbuckle/OpenAPI on the host that actually serves the 1,306-endpoint legacy surface and publish the generated spec as a build artifact.
recommended_advantages: Produces a complete, authoritative, machine-readable surface automatically; cannot drift because it is generated from the running code; replaces four disagreeing artefacts (catalogue 1,306, docs 452 routes, Swagger 690, snapshot 48) with one; unblocks generated request and response validation at the same time.
recommended_disadvantages: Requires a change on the API host, which is outside this snapshot and outside QA's control; needs a build-pipeline change to publish the artifact; legacy controllers may need attribute routing before Swashbuckle can enumerate them.
recommended_effort: M - 1-3 weeks of development effort on the API host, then near-zero maintenance
alternative_solution: Ask development for a per-build route dump (a startup hook or CI step that serialises the registered route table to JSON) instead of a full OpenAPI spec.
alternative_advantages: Very small change; settles what exists on which build; immediately eliminates the 135 endpoints that return 404; can be diffed in CI against APIConfig.java to prevent recurrence.
alternative_disadvantages: Gives routes only - no schemas, no response models, no error codes, so it closes the surface question and none of the contract questions; leaves the create blocker fully in place.

issue: 58 of the 70 declared controllers have no implementation anywhere in pam/PAM - no matching *Controller.cs class, and not one declared action present as a public method. Only 12 controllers have any implementation, and only OfflineSync is complete.
recommended_solution: Have development identify and document, per controller, which component and host serves it - a one-page ownership map covering all 70 controllers.
recommended_advantages: Tells QA where each surface actually lives so the right source can be requested per controller; makes the legacy-versus-microservices split explicit; cheap and needs no code change; prerequisite for deciding which surfaces are worth automating.
recommended_disadvantages: A static document that will rot as components move; relies on developer knowledge that may itself be incomplete for the oldest controllers.
alternative_solution: Derive ownership empirically from the API gateway routing configuration and per-controller response headers observed in the existing run evidence, rather than asking.
alternative_advantages: No dependency on developer availability; based on observed behaviour rather than recollection; reuses the 1,868 evidence files already captured.
alternative_disadvantages: Requires gateway configuration access we do not have; headers may not identify the backing component; produces inference rather than an authoritative statement.
alternative_effort: M - 1-3 weeks, and may fail to resolve

issue: pam/PAM exposes no machine-readable contract: no Swagger/Swashbuckle registration and no route attributes in the Framework projects, so even the 48 endpoints present yield nothing a generator can consume.
recommended_solution: Add attribute routing plus Swashbuckle to the Framework projects that do serve HTTP, so the surface becomes self-describing at the source.
recommended_advantages: Makes the contract a property of the code rather than a document; generated docs stay correct by construction; benefits developers and consumers as well as QA.
recommended_disadvantages: Touches legacy projects with regression risk; convention-based routing may need refactoring before attributes work; only covers the 8 controller-bearing projects in this snapshot, not the separately hosted surface.
alternative_solution: Keep APIConfig.java as the declared surface and add a CI job that diffs it against a per-build route dump, treating any divergence as a build warning.
alternative_advantages: No product code change; makes drift visible immediately; QA owns it end to end so it needs no external approval; would have caught the Se0rviceDetailsV3 typo and the 135 false 404s.
alternative_disadvantages: Still no schemas or response models; keeps a hand-maintained catalogue as the baseline, which is how the typos and stale entries arose.
owner_team: Development, or QA Automation for the alternative

issue: Only 3 of 6,738 public properties in pam/PAM carry any validation attribute. All three are [Required], all three sit in one file (ARCON_Services/ProvisioningService/ProvisioningDataAccessLayer/Models/Entity.cs), and none belongs to a catalogue endpoint. Of 56 mandatory-field hints in the merged source map, 0 are backed by a declaration and only 1 of 217 create endpoints has one.
recommended_solution: Supply a read-only INFORMATION_SCHEMA export for the QA database - columns, NOT NULL, data types, lengths, foreign keys and CHECK constraints - as CSV.
recommended_advantages: Recovers mandatory-ness, types, lengths and valid enum values in one artifact; the constraints demonstrably exist in the database even though the models omit them; a one-off export grants no standing access, so the security objection disappears; directly targets the 204 failing creates.
recommended_disadvantages: A point-in-time snapshot that goes stale; database column names do not always match API field names, so a mapping step is still needed; does not capture rules enforced in procedural code rather than constraints.
recommended_effort: S - 1-3 days for the DBA to export
alternative_solution: Annotate the request models with [Required] and length/range attributes, starting with the most-used create endpoints.
alternative_advantages: The durable fix - metadata lives with the code, cannot drift, and simultaneously enables server-side validation and generated documentation; already raised as LH-10.
alternative_disadvantages: Slow and incremental across 6,738 properties; needs developer effort per model; risks changing runtime behaviour if validation begins rejecting requests that previously passed; most catalogue endpoints are not in this snapshot to annotate.
owner_team: DBA/Infrastructure for the recommendation, Development for the alternative

issue: Zero length, format, pattern or range constraints exist anywhere in 110.9 M characters of product source - no StringLength, MaxLength, MinLength or Range attribute occurs even once. Boundary and format negative cases therefore have no derivable expectation.
recommended_solution: Recover constraints from the database schema (VARCHAR lengths, numeric precision, CHECK constraints) as part of the A6-04 export, and generate boundary cases from those limits.
recommended_advantages: One export serves both mandatory-ness and constraints; column lengths are authoritative for storage limits; enables generated at-limit and over-limit cases where today there are none; no product code change.
recommended_disadvantages: Database limits may be wider than the intended business limits, so a passing over-limit case is not proof of correctness; formats and patterns (email, IP, GUID) are usually not expressed as CHECK constraints.
recommended_effort: S - 1-3 days once the schema export exists
alternative_solution: Build a differential baseline: probe field limits through observed behaviour, freeze the responses as the expected contract, and alert on change.
alternative_advantages: Requires nothing from anyone else; captures real enforced behaviour including undocumented rules; detects regressions even without a specification.
alternative_disadvantages: Freezes current behaviour as correct, defects included; cannot detect 'this should have been rejected and was not'; probing requires write traffic against a shared environment, which is currently restricted.

issue: No response model or DTO in pam/PAM is bound to a route, and no envelope type is declared, so the expected response cannot be derived from the source. 31 distinct response shapes were measured live against 6 documented.
recommended_solution: Declare a single versioned response envelope type in the API and reference it from every operation, with the Result payload typed per operation.
recommended_advantages: Collapses 31 observed shapes toward a small declared set; makes response assertions generatable; benefits every API consumer, not only QA; surfaces automatically once Swashbuckle is enabled (A6-01).
recommended_disadvantages: A breaking change for existing consumers relying on current shapes; substantial refactoring across the surface; needs a deprecation window and version negotiation.
alternative_solution: Leave the API unchanged and publish a shape catalogue: enumerate the 31 observed shapes, state which endpoints return which, and define the success test for each.
alternative_advantages: No product change and no consumer breakage; QA can author the first draft from the existing 1,868 evidence files; immediately makes shape-tolerant assertions correct rather than defensive guesses.
alternative_disadvantages: Documents inconsistency instead of fixing it; must be maintained as shapes change; leaves each new endpoint free to invent a 32nd shape.

issue: pam/PAM is a consumer of the PAM API, not its implementation - APIParam.PAMAPIURL is referenced 123 times and PAMAPIToken 54 times, the base URL is loaded from a settings row at CommonFunctionsCM.cs:17063, and routes appear only as client call-site string literals. Treating the snapshot as the server misdirects any planning built on it.
recommended_solution: Record the client-versus-server distinction explicitly in the workspace guidance so no future plan assumes the API can be parsed from this tree, and reclassify the snapshot as a reference for types and call patterns only.
recommended_advantages: Prevents repeated wasted analysis; costs nothing; makes the 3.7% figure interpretable rather than merely alarming; preserves the repository's genuine value instead of discarding it.
recommended_disadvantages: Documentation-only - changes no capability; relies on future readers actually consulting the guidance.
alternative_solution: Request the source of the components that actually serve the legacy surface, so the contract can be derived statically after all.
alternative_advantages: Would allow genuine static derivation of routes, models and validation for the full surface; removes the dependency on live probing.
alternative_disadvantages: Explicitly out of scope in docs/gaps/02-Data-Access-Requests.md §9; a large access ask that a generated spec (A6-01) makes unnecessary; more source would still not mark mandatory fields if those models are equally unannotated.
alternative_effort: L - procurement and access, 1-3 months, likely refused
owner_team: QA Automation for the recommendation, Development for the alternative

issue: 13 of the 25 *Controller classes in pam/PAM are not catalogue controllers, and three of those (HelloController, ValuesController, HomeController) are ASP.NET project-template scaffolding. Counting controllers without inspecting them overstates the repository's API presence by roughly half.
recommended_solution: Always report controller presence as an intersection with the declared catalogue, never as a raw class count, and keep the scaffolding classes named in the analysis so the distinction survives.
recommended_advantages: Removes a recurring source of inflated figures; already implemented in measure_doc_gap.py; makes the 12-of-70 result reproducible by anyone.
recommended_disadvantages: None material - a reporting convention rather than a change in capability.
alternative_solution: Ask development to delete the unused template controllers from the product source.
alternative_advantages: Removes dead code and any unintended endpoints the templates expose; reduces attack surface if they are reachable in a deployed build.
alternative_disadvantages: Product change with no QA benefit beyond tidiness; requires regression testing; scaffolding may be harmless if never routed.
owner_team: QA Automation for the recommendation, Development for the alternative

issue: The widely cited '54 of 70 controllers absent' figure was never measured. It is a hardcoded string literal emitted by build_source_map.py:333 into the generated SOURCE-MAP.md, from where docs/gaps/01-Data-Gap-Analysis.md inherited it. Because the file is auto-generated, the number survived every regeneration while appearing authoritative. The correct figure is 58.
recommended_solution: Prohibit hardcoded figures in generator output: every number a script prints must be computed in that run, and any narrative constant must cite its source file instead of restating a value.
recommended_advantages: Removes an entire class of false-authority defect; cheap to enforce by review; the auto-generated provenance is exactly what made this figure hard to challenge; also fixes the same pattern at lh_specs_run.py:944,1046.
recommended_disadvantages: Some genuinely external constants must still be cited by hand; requires discipline rather than tooling, so it can lapse.
recommended_effort: S - 1-3 days to fix the two known scripts and regenerate
alternative_solution: Add an assertion harness that recomputes every headline figure quoted in the workspace documentation and fails when a document disagrees with the measurement.
alternative_advantages: Catches drift automatically and continuously, not only where someone remembers to look; would have flagged 23-vs-54, 4-vs-3 error codes, 8-vs-31 shapes and 1,322-vs-1,306 at once.
alternative_disadvantages: Needs a parseable convention for figures inside prose, which does not exist today; meaningful build effort; risks false alarms where two figures legitimately differ by definition, as 22 and 58 do here.

issue: docs/gaps/01-Data-Gap-Analysis.md §3.1 is internally inconsistent: it states 217 create endpoints, 138 with a request body from any source, and 101 with no body derivable anywhere. 138 + 101 = 239 > 217. Recomputed from source-map.json the correct figure is 79, not 101; the same 101 is repeated in docs/briefs/document-gap.md §5.
recommended_solution: Correct both documents to 79 and state the complement explicitly (138 with + 79 without = 217) so the arithmetic is self-checking on the page.
recommended_advantages: Fixes a figure that understates the recoverable create population by 22 endpoints; showing the complement makes any future inconsistency visible at a glance; a small edit to two files.
recommended_disadvantages: Does not prevent the same error recurring elsewhere; requires touching two documents that other reports cite.
alternative_solution: Stop quoting create-coverage figures in prose and have both documents reference artifacts/analysis-data/doc-gap-coverage.json and source-map.json as the single computed source.
alternative_advantages: Removes hand-copied figures permanently; one place to update; consistent with the A6-09 fix.
alternative_disadvantages: Makes the documents less readable standalone; a reader without the JSON to hand loses the headline; management-facing summaries do need the number inline.

issue: The missing mandatory-field metadata cascades into three measured failures that are one defect: 204 of 217 creates fail, producing 196 L5 failures all carrying the identical detail 'resolved []; MISSING [NEW_ID]', which leaves nothing to read back so L6 record-exists passes only 2 of 107, and 296 of 326 flows FAIL.
recommended_solution: Treat it as one defect and fix it at the root: obtain mandatory-field metadata (A6-04), repair the create bodies, and re-run so the chain depth, read-back and persistence measures move together.
recommended_advantages: One remediation closes three reported symptoms; the mechanism is already proven to 5 hops with no hardcoded values, so no tooling work is needed; progress is measurable in the next run against a known baseline of 13 of 217.
recommended_disadvantages: Entirely blocked on an external dependency - no amount of QA work advances it; re-running needs a valid token and the service account is currently locked.
recommended_effort: S - 1-3 days of QA work once metadata arrives
alternative_solution: Decouple chain testing from creation: seed a known, reserved set of records once, then chain from those fixed identifiers rather than from freshly created ones.
alternative_advantages: Unblocks chaining depth and read-back immediately without any metadata; gives assertable preconditions and repeatability; AUTOMATION_TEST_LOB already exists and could be formalised as reserved.
alternative_disadvantages: Leaves create coverage itself untested, which is the larger risk; seeded data drifts on a shared environment; needs a restore mechanism and a guarantee other teams will not modify the records.
alternative_effort: M - 1-3 weeks, needs QA plus Infrastructure

issue: docs/findings/issues/ISSUE-005-api-coverage-gap.md quotes 1,322 endpoints throughout (§2, §3, §4, §6). The authoritative catalogue count is 1,306; 1,322 and 1,336 are stale.
recommended_solution: Add a superseding note at the head of ISSUE-005 stating that 1,306 is the current count and that the issue's percentages were computed against 1,322, leaving the original text intact as the historical record.
recommended_advantages: Preserves the append-only discipline for issued analysis while stopping the stale figure propagating; minimal edit; the issue's conclusion about two disjoint surfaces is unaffected either way.
recommended_disadvantages: Leaves incorrect figures visible in the body; a reader skimming the tables still sees 1,322.
alternative_solution: Recompute and reissue ISSUE-005 against 1,306, including the ~6% Swagger overlap percentages.
alternative_advantages: Every figure in the document becomes correct; the overlap percentages shift slightly and would be restated accurately.
alternative_disadvantages: Rewrites issued analysis, breaking traceability for anyone who cited the original; the conclusion does not change, so the effort buys little.

issue: 912 of 1,306 catalogue endpoints (69.8%) have no exact-route reference anywhere in the 2,470-page Confluence export. 18 of 70 controllers have no documented endpoint at all, and 17 controllers covering 410 endpoints have neither documentation nor implementation.
recommended_solution: Generate the reference from the running API (OpenAPI per build) rather than authoring the missing 912 by hand, so coverage becomes complete by construction.
recommended_advantages: Closes a 912-endpoint gap that no writing programme would realistically finish; cannot fall behind the build; simultaneously delivers schemas, response models and error responses; converts documentation from a project into a pipeline property.
recommended_disadvantages: Generated reference lacks the narrative and business context the current export provides; needs the host change in A6-01 first; auto-generated docs are only as good as the annotations behind them.
recommended_effort: M - 1-3 weeks on the API host
alternative_solution: Publish a minimal one-line-per-endpoint table for the missing 912 - route, verb, controller, one-line purpose - and defer full prose.
alternative_advantages: Achievable by the documentation team without any code change; a route plus verb plus purpose is enough to make an endpoint discoverable and testable at read level; can be produced from the catalogue in bulk and reviewed incrementally.
alternative_disadvantages: Still no schemas, mandatory flags, response models or error codes, so it does not unblock write coverage; hand-maintained, so it starts rotting immediately; 912 rows is a substantial review burden.
owner_team: Development for the recommendation, Documentation for the alternative

issue: The versioned controller families are almost entirely undocumented: 10 controllers covering 562 of 1,306 endpoints (43.0% of the surface) have 1 documented endpoint between them (0.2%) and 1 implementation in pam/PAM. ServiceDetailsV2 (132 endpoints) and ServiceDetailsV3 (123) are the two largest controllers in the catalogue and have zero documented endpoints, while their unversioned originals are well documented.
recommended_solution: Require documentation of the current version as a release gate, and mark each endpoint with a status - active, deprecated or planned - plus the version it applies to.
recommended_advantages: Directly addresses the pattern where each version bump shipped without documentation; tells testers which of V1/V2/V3/V4 to target, currently unanswerable; prevents the gap widening with the next version; the highest-value 43% of the surface benefits first.
recommended_disadvantages: Adds a release gate that development must accept; does not retrospectively document the existing 562 endpoints; requires someone to adjudicate which versions are actually current.
recommended_effort: M - 1-3 weeks to define and adopt the gate
alternative_solution: Ask development a single prior question - are the V2/V3/V4 families current and the unversioned ones deprecated, or the reverse - and target automation and documentation at whichever surface is live, freezing the other.
alternative_advantages: One question may remove 562 endpoints from scope or conversely redirect the whole effort; extremely cheap; prevents investing in a surface being retired; mirrors the highest-value open question already recorded in ISSUE-005 §6.
alternative_disadvantages: If the answer is 'both are live' nothing is resolved and the full documentation gap remains; relies on a definitive answer existing.
alternative_effort: XS - hours to ask, days to receive

issue: No field is marked mandatory anywhere in the 2,470-page export, and the product declares only 3 [Required] attributes across 6,738 properties, none on a catalogue endpoint. Mandatory-ness is therefore inferred from 'appears in every documented example' - 56 such hints exist, 0 backed by a declaration, and only 1 of 217 create endpoints has one.
recommended_solution: Publish a per-endpoint field table: field, type, mandatory flag, example value, and constraint. Generated from the OpenAPI spec where it exists, authored for the rest, most-used creates first.
recommended_advantages: Converts the export from a reading reference into a machine-consumable contract; single change with the largest measured effect, moving creates from 13 of 217 upward; twenty annotated endpoints would be visible in the next run; also enables generated negative cases for missing-mandatory-field.
recommended_disadvantages: Substantial authoring effort if not generated; hand-authored tables rot; needs a decision on where the table lives so it does not fork from the code.
recommended_effort: M - 1-3 weeks for the top endpoints, L for full coverage
alternative_solution: Recover mandatory-ness from database NOT NULL constraints via the schema export in A6-04, and treat the derived set as the working contract until a declared one exists.
alternative_advantages: Fast and needs no writing; the database cannot be as permissive as the models suggest and still function, so the information is genuinely there; one export covers all endpoints at once rather than incrementally.
alternative_disadvantages: Column names do not always match API field names; NOT NULL is not identical to API-mandatory since a field may be defaulted server-side; misses rules enforced only in procedural code; produces inference that cannot be cited as a contract.
alternative_effort: S - 1-3 days once the export arrives
owner_team: Development + Documentation, DBA for the alternative

issue: The 2,470-page export documents 3 distinct error-code values (only 2 in ARCON NNN-XXX-YYY format) against 108 observed live, and 351 of the 358 ErrorCode field occurrences (98.0%) are null - the export shows almost exclusively the success path. Only 2 of 70 controllers have any documented error code, and the framework hardcodes just {201, 202, 203}.
recommended_solution: Publish a complete error-code register: code, meaning, emitting endpoints, client action, and category (client fault versus server fault). QA has already derived all 108 codes with representative messages, so development confirms and completes rather than authoring from scratch.
recommended_advantages: The single highest-value documentation change available - without it success cannot be determined at all; unblocks negative testing end to end and lets the 3,317 existing negative rows carry a real ExpectedErrorCode instead of the 0 they carry today; the derivation work is already done in LH-04 EVIDENCE.xlsx; the category column also drives the correct HTTP status decision in A7-06.
recommended_disadvantages: Requires developer time to confirm meanings that are currently inferred from message text, which is precisely the weakness; must also normalise the 17 malformed codes (missing separators, trailing dashes, no numeric prefix, four with a stack trace concatenated into the code field); needs an owner to keep it current as codes are added.
recommended_effort: M - 1-3 weeks of developer review of a QA-supplied draft
alternative_solution: Freeze the QA-derived 108-code table as a provisional register, wire it into the framework in place of the hardcoded {201, 202, 203}, and treat any unrecognised code as a failure requiring triage.
alternative_advantages: Needs nothing from development and can ship immediately; makes every new or unrecognised code visible instead of silently passing; replaces a 3-element hardcoded set with 108 real values; a new code appearing becomes a signal rather than a blind spot.
alternative_disadvantages: Meanings remain inferred from message text and may be wrong; freezes current behaviour including defects; no coverage of codes not yet observed; a QA-owned register carries no authority with development.
owner_team: Development, with the draft supplied by QA Automation

issue: The previously reported figure of 4 documented error codes is wrong: 190-SSH and 100-SSH are false positives, being fragments of ServiceDisplayName values such as '10.11.10.190@preeti:10.11.10.190-SSH LINUX' at pam-api:p1065 and p1066. A third such artefact, 214-SSH at p1064, was never reported, and the genuine code APA:UR0021 at p2441 was missed. The corrected count is 3 values, 2 in ARCON format.
recommended_solution: Extract error codes from the value of an ErrorCode field rather than by pattern-matching free text, and where prose matching is unavoidable apply a negative lookbehind for a preceding digit or dot so dotted-quad fragments cannot match.
recommended_advantages: Eliminates the false-positive class entirely and found a genuine code the pattern approach missed; the field-value method also yields the 351-null measurement, which is a stronger finding than the code count itself; implemented and documented at measure_doc_gap.py:196.
recommended_disadvantages: Field extraction misses codes mentioned only in prose, so both methods are still needed; the malformed codes without a numeric prefix remain hard to match by shape alone.
alternative_solution: Validate every extracted code against the QA-derived 108-code register and reject anything not on it.
alternative_advantages: Uses a known-good vocabulary rather than a shape heuristic, so precision is near-perfect; trivially catches IP fragments.
alternative_disadvantages: Circular for discovery - cannot find a code the register does not already contain, which is exactly what happened with APA:UR0021; the register itself is unconfirmed.

issue: Status-code semantics are undefined. Across 2,470 pages there are 104 incidental HTTP status mentions (200 x46, 400 x21, 401 x12, 500 x11, 201 x5, 404 x3, 503 x3, 403 x2, 405 x1) and nowhere a statement of what any status means for this API. In reality a rejected request returns HTTP 200 with an application error in the body - 289 of 1,868 calls returned 200 with Success: false.
recommended_solution: Take an explicit architectural decision and publish it: either map error-code class to a real HTTP status (client-fault to 4xx, server-fault to 500), or formally adopt the envelope as the contract and document how to determine success for each shape.
recommended_advantages: Either answer makes assertions non-provisional, which the status quo does not; mapping to real statuses makes standard tooling, monitoring and client retry logic work correctly; the decision is cheap even though implementing the first option is not; already proposed inside PAMIT-42744.
recommended_disadvantages: Changing statuses breaks existing consumers that treat 200 as transport success and needs a deprecation window; adopting the envelope instead requires the error register (A7-04) and the shape catalogue (A6-06) to exist before it is testable.
recommended_effort: XS for the decision, L - 1-3 months to implement the status mapping
alternative_solution: Change nothing in the API and add one prominent paragraph to the documentation stating that HTTP 200 does not indicate success and that Success and ErrorCode must be read.
alternative_advantages: Lowest-effort item in this entire analysis and prevents a whole class of false-green testing; no code change and no consumer breakage; immediately corrects the most dangerous misreading a new tester can make.
alternative_disadvantages: Documents the problem rather than fixing it; standard tooling and monitoring still misreport rejected requests as successes; leaves every assertion dependent on the envelope being documented.
owner_team: Architecture + Development, Documentation for the alternative

issue: 31 distinct response shapes were measured across 1,868 executed calls and only 6 match a shape the documentation describes, yet the export presents the envelope as uniform. Only 159 of 3,194 documented JSON examples (5.0%) are response-shaped at all, and 33 of 70 controllers have no response example whatsoever.
recommended_solution: Document every envelope variant with, for each, the endpoints that use it and the explicit test for success - including the pathological cases where the error is embedded in a pipe-delimited string inside a JSON field, where the body is a bare array, and where Result is an object rather than an array.
recommended_advantages: Makes shape-tolerant assertions correct by design rather than defensive; directly addresses the 590 L3 envelope failures, the largest single failure class after L4; can be drafted from the 1,868 evidence files already captured, so it needs discovery rather than invention.
recommended_disadvantages: Documents inconsistency instead of removing it; must be maintained as new shapes appear; 31 variants is itself a signal that the underlying design needs the fix in A6-06.
alternative_solution: Publish a machine-readable response schema per operation as part of the OpenAPI spec, letting the shape be declared per endpoint rather than catalogued centrally.
alternative_advantages: Per-operation schemas are directly consumable by generated assertions with no central catalogue to maintain; cannot drift from the code; handles the long tail of one-off shapes naturally.
alternative_disadvantages: Depends entirely on A6-01 landing first; a generated schema records the current shape without flagging that 31 variants is a defect; the pathological string-embedded-error case is representable in OpenAPI only as an opaque string.

issue: Documented payloads are bound to their endpoint only by page proximity, because the export lists a route as a heading with the payload beneath it. 1,589 of 3,194 parsed JSON objects (49.7%) are orphaned with no endpoint near enough to bind, and every one of the 1,605 bindings is a hypothesis that may be wrong.
recommended_solution: Restructure the export so each payload is explicitly labelled with its endpoint - a route heading immediately above each request and response block, with the words Request and Response stated - so binding becomes deterministic rather than positional.
recommended_advantages: Makes the export's single greatest asset, its 3,194 payload examples, machine-consumable; recovers up to 1,589 currently unusable examples; a structural change to how pages are authored rather than new content; removes the caveat that currently attaches to every payload-derived figure.
recommended_disadvantages: Requires reworking 2,470 pages of existing Confluence content; the owner has already confirmed the source is not up to date, so effort may be spent restructuring stale material; does not add any missing information.
alternative_solution: Leave the export as it is and improve the extraction instead: use heading hierarchy and Request/Response keyword anchors rather than page proximity, and emit a confidence score per binding.
alternative_advantages: QA-owned and needs nothing from anyone; a scored binding is honest about uncertainty in a way the current all-or-nothing approach is not; likely recovers a large share of the 1,589 orphans; build_source_map.py already carries a confidence model to extend.
alternative_disadvantages: Still inference and still sometimes wrong; heading structure may not survive PDF extraction cleanly; effort is spent working around a source defect rather than fixing it.
owner_team: Documentation for the recommendation, QA Automation for the alternative

issue: Documented payload examples carry no field types, lengths, formats, patterns or value constraints, so an identifier cannot be distinguished from free text and no boundary case can be generated. Combined with zero constraint attributes in the product source, no source available describes any field limit.
recommended_solution: Extend the per-endpoint field table (A7-03) to carry type, format, pattern and length for every property, sourced from the OpenAPI schema where it exists.
recommended_advantages: Enables generated boundary, format and invalid-type negative cases that are impossible today; resolves the observed ServiceId string-on-create versus integer-on-read ambiguity by declaring it; one table serves mandatory-ness and constraints together.
recommended_disadvantages: Only as good as the annotations behind it, and there are currently 3; needs the model annotation or schema work in A6-04 and A6-05 to have real values to publish.
alternative_solution: Infer types from the 2,674 C# property types already mapped from pam/PAM, plus the observed example values, and publish the inferred register with confidence marked.
alternative_advantages: Uses assets already in hand and already merged in source-map.json; C# types are authoritative for type even where mandatory-ness is not; immediately fixes the string-versus-integer casting problem for the fields it covers.
alternative_disadvantages: Types only - no lengths, formats or patterns, since none exist in the source; covers only fields whose names appear in pam/PAM; name-based matching can bind the wrong property where names collide.

issue: No workflow, ordering or dependency information exists anywhere. All 2,470 pages were scanned for 17 ordering phrases - must first, before calling, after creating, prerequisite, in the following order, step 1, returned by the previous, obtained from the and further variants - and 0 pages contain any of them. Correspondingly all 1,680 chain candidates were derived by field-name matching and 0 came from documentation or an observed producer response.
recommended_solution: Publish a dependency map per write endpoint: what must exist beforehand, which identifier the call returns, and which endpoints consume that identifier.
recommended_advantages: Replaces field-name guessing with declared relationships, directly addressing the 196 identical MISSING [NEW_ID] failures; makes multi-hop generation deterministic instead of inferential; the mechanism is already proven to 5 hops, so declared dependencies convert straight into working chains; also documents the product's real usage sequences for developers.
recommended_disadvantages: Requires developer knowledge of cross-controller relationships that may not be written down anywhere; a large surface to cover across 217 creates; the map must be maintained as endpoints change.
recommended_effort: L - 1-3 months for full coverage, M for the top flows
alternative_solution: Derive the dependency graph empirically: once creates succeed, record which identifier each producer actually returns and which consumer accepts it, and promote confirmed pairs from name-inferred to observed.
alternative_advantages: Self-building and needs nothing from development; observed pairs are stronger evidence than a document; the harness already models chain candidates so only the promotion step is new; converts the 0-of-1,680 observed figure upward with every run.
alternative_disadvantages: Blocked behind the create fix in A6-04 - with 13 of 217 creates working there is little to observe; discovers only relationships the harness happens to exercise; cannot distinguish a coincidental field-name match from a real contract.

issue: Business rules the product demonstrably enforces are documented nowhere: 42 of 70 controllers have no constraint language on any documented page. Most dangerously, POST /api/ServiceCreation/SetServiceDetails returns Success: true with Message: 'Already Exists' when nothing was inserted, so a create assertion checking both the status code and the Success flag still passes when no record was written.
recommended_solution: Document the success semantics of every write operation explicitly: which Message values mean the record was created, which mean no-op, and which mean partial success - and state that Success: true alone is not evidence of a write.
recommended_advantages: Prevents false-green results on the most important class of test there is; the rule is already relied on by the harness and would otherwise remain tribal knowledge; small and targeted, covering write endpoints only; directly addresses the 458 L4 message-semantics failures.
recommended_disadvantages: Message strings are a fragile contract and may be localised or reworded; documenting them entrenches string matching rather than fixing the underlying signal; needs per-endpoint review of write operations.
alternative_solution: Fix the signal rather than document it: return a distinct errorCode or a created-versus-existing indicator so no-op and insert are machine-distinguishable without parsing prose.
alternative_advantages: Removes the string-matching dependency permanently; makes the distinction assertable by any consumer; the correct long-term design and consistent with the A7-04 register.
alternative_disadvantages: Changes response behaviour, so existing consumers relying on Success: true must be reviewed; needs the error register and status decision settled first; longer path to the same testing outcome.

issue: The endpoint catalogue itself contains defects, so documentation cannot be reconciled against a clean baseline: a typo'd controller /api/Se0rviceDetailsV3/SetServiceSessionLogoutV2 (APIConfig.java:893) that produces a hard 404; a double-slash typo hiding the real AzureKeyVault/GetDatabaseStatus (APIConfig.java:188); a version segment v1.0 parsed as a controller across 3 endpoints; 4 endpoints declared with unsubstituted {id} placeholders; and 7 with hardcoded environment-specific query strings including literal GUIDs and ?TicketId=LAMTest123.
recommended_solution: Add a CI validation step over APIConfig.java that fails on a malformed route, an unsubstituted placeholder, a hardcoded query-string literal, or a duplicate declaration, and fix the 15 known defects.
recommended_advantages: Cheap, entirely QA-owned, and prevents recurrence rather than just fixing the current instances; would have caught both typos at commit time; removes a category of guaranteed-failing tests that currently pollute the pass rate; placeholders and hardcoded ids are latent failures waiting on an environment change.
recommended_disadvantages: Does not resolve which of the 135 declared-but-404 endpoints are genuinely wrong versus genuinely missing from the build - that needs A6-01; some hardcoded query values may be deliberate probes needing individual review.
alternative_solution: Replace the hand-maintained APIConfig.java with a catalogue generated from the per-build route dump, eliminating hand-typed routes altogether.
alternative_advantages: Removes the entire class of transcription defects permanently; keeps the catalogue automatically in step with the deployed build; would also resolve the 135 false 404s and the 210 Excel-only endpoints as a side effect.
alternative_disadvantages: Depends on development supplying the route dump; a substantial refactor of a file referenced throughout the framework; loses the hand-curated constant names that existing tests bind to.

issue: 210 endpoints present in the positive test Excel are absent from APIConfig.java, mostly the SCIM Service/* and User/* surface. The test data files therefore describe a surface the catalogue does not declare, so coverage figures quoted against the catalogue silently exclude them.
recommended_solution: Reconcile the two sources into one declared surface: add the 210 to APIConfig.java where they are live, mark them deprecated where they are not, and add a CI check that the Excel and the catalogue cannot diverge again.
recommended_advantages: Makes any coverage percentage trustworthy, which it currently is not; brings the SCIM surface into scope explicitly rather than by accident; the CI check stops recurrence; resolves which artifact is authoritative when they disagree.
recommended_disadvantages: Requires deciding the status of 210 endpoints, which needs development input; growing the catalogue grows the surface the run must cover and the runtime with it.
alternative_solution: Treat the SCIM surface as a separate programme with its own catalogue and coverage figure, and state the split explicitly wherever coverage is reported.
alternative_advantages: Honest immediately without waiting on reconciliation; SCIM is a genuinely different surface with its own conventions, so separate treatment may be correct; avoids inflating the legacy catalogue with endpoints that follow different rules.
alternative_disadvantages: Two catalogues to maintain and two figures to quote, which invites exactly the confusion this issue describes; defers rather than resolves the question of which surface is authoritative.

issue: Four artefacts disagree about what the API is - the catalogue declares 1,306 endpoints, the documentation cites 452 routes, the shared Swagger specs describe 690 operations with roughly 6% name overlap, and the product snapshot contains 48 - and none is authoritative. 135 declared endpoints returned HTTP 404 live, and the documentation cannot arbitrate because it is not versioned against a build.
recommended_solution: Establish the per-build generated route list as the single authoritative surface, and have every other artifact - catalogue, documentation, test data - reconcile against it in CI.
recommended_advantages: Replaces four disagreeing sources with one that cannot be wrong about the deployed build; permanently eliminates the 135 false 404s; makes the catalogue, Excel and documentation all checkable rather than merely assertable; the only remediation that prevents its own problem recurring.
recommended_disadvantages: Depends on development supplying the route dump or spec; a build-specific surface means the catalogue must be branch-aware, adding CI complexity; does not retrospectively explain which of the four historical figures was right.
alternative_solution: Keep the catalogue authoritative and annotate each of the 135 endpoints returning 404 with an observed status, refreshing that annotation on every run.
alternative_advantages: Entirely QA-owned and needs nothing external; makes the discrepancy visible per endpoint rather than as an aggregate; the run already captures the evidence needed.
alternative_disadvantages: Records the symptom rather than resolving it; cannot distinguish 'never existed' from 'removed in this build' from 'typo in the catalogue'; annotation goes stale on every deployment.

issue: The export carries no version and marks no endpoint status, and the owner has confirmed it is not up to date. A reader cannot tell which PAM release the document applies to, nor whether a given endpoint is active, deprecated or planned - which is what allowed 562 versioned endpoints to go undocumented while the document continued describing their predecessors.
recommended_solution: Version the document against a PAM release, and mark every endpoint with a status of active, deprecated or planned plus the version in which it appeared.
recommended_advantages: Lets a reader know what applies to the build in front of them, which is currently unanswerable; makes staleness visible instead of invisible; the status flag directly addresses the V1-versus-V2/V3/V4 ambiguity in A7-02; low effort relative to its clarifying value.
recommended_disadvantages: Adds a maintenance obligation per release that the current process has not sustained; a version label on stale content does not make it accurate, only honestly labelled.
alternative_solution: Retire the hand-maintained export as the API reference, keep it only for narrative and business context, and let the generated OpenAPI spec carry the contract with the build version embedded.
alternative_advantages: Versioning becomes automatic and cannot lapse; separates the two things the document currently conflates - business explanation, which humans should write, and contract, which machines should generate; removes the upkeep burden entirely.
alternative_disadvantages: Depends on A6-01; discards the reference role of an asset with 3,194 payload examples before the replacement is proven; the narrative content still needs versioning to stay useful.

issue: Eleven workspace documents carry figures this analysis re-measured as wrong: the 23-versus-54 controller absence (correct value 58), 4 documented error codes (3), 101 creates with no body (79), 8 response shapes (31), and 1,322 endpoints (1,306). Two of these figures are hardcoded strings inside generator scripts, so they regenerate unchanged.
recommended_solution: Apply the corrections listed in A7 §9 in one pass, fix the two hardcoded generator strings first so regeneration cannot reintroduce them, then regenerate the derived files.
recommended_advantages: Removes every known incorrect figure at once and in the right order, so generated files do not overwrite the fixes; the correction table already names each file and line, so the work is mechanical; leaves the frozen archive untouched as the rules require.
recommended_disadvantages: Touches many files including issued Jira evidence packs, which need regeneration rather than editing; a one-off pass with no guarantee against the next divergence.
alternative_solution: Leave the prose figures in place and add a single authoritative figures file that every document references, deprecating inline numbers over time.
alternative_advantages: One place to update permanently; makes divergence structurally impossible for anything that references it; complements the A6-09 no-hardcoded-figures rule.
alternative_disadvantages: Leaves known-wrong numbers visible in the meantime; management-facing documents genuinely need figures inline to read well; migrating every document is slower than fixing eleven values.
